message:
fix(release): bundle frozen engine into release artifacts, fix pre-checkout tag verify cwd (#244/#250) (#254)

Co-authored-by: Devin <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

entries.text:
name: Release

# Tag push (v*) or manual dispatch builds the desktop app on a hosted
# Windows runner (MSVC toolchain is preinstalled there) and publishes the
# NSIS installer + a portable zip to a GitHub Release.  #244: the
# frozen transcription engine (PyInstaller onefile, ~130 MB) is built
# and smoke-tested here too — the bundled config ships it inside the
# installer and beside the portable exe so transcription works on a
# machine with no Python at all.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "Existing tag to release (v0.1.0 or 0.1.0)"
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  # #216: normalize the dispatch input — "0.1.0" and "v0.1.0" both mean
  # the v-prefixed tag. Push triggers already carry the full ref name.
  RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag && (startsWith(inputs.tag, 'v') && inputs.tag || format('v{0}', inputs.tag)) || github.ref_name }}

jobs:
  windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/desktop
    steps:
      - name: Verify tag exists
        shell: bash
        # #250: this step runs BEFORE checkout, so the job-level
        # apps/desktop working-directory does not exist yet — the
        # workspace root does.
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/git/ref/tags/${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}" --silent || {
            echo "::error::tag ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }} does not exist — create it first (git tag ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }} && git push --tags)"
            exit 1
          }

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/desktop/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/desktop/src-tauri

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          # ENGINE_RUNTIME_MATRIX.md: Python 3.12 + ONNX Runtime is
          # the measured-good engine runtime (plain pip install of
          # basic-pitch fails on 3.12 — see the --no-deps step).
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Verify tag matches app version
        shell: bash
        run: |
          TAG="${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}"
          TAG="${TAG#v}"
          PKG=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          CONF=$(node -p "require('./src-tauri/tauri.conf.json').version")
          [ "$TAG" = "$PKG" ] && [ "$TAG" = "$CONF" ] || {
            echo "::error::tag v$TAG != package.json $PKG / tauri.conf.json $CONF — bump versions first"
            exit 1
          }

      - name: Install frontend deps
        run: npm ci

      - name: Typecheck + unit tests
        run: npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run

      - name: Rust tests
        working-directory: apps/desktop/src-tauri
        run: cargo test --locked

      - name: Python engine tests
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          pip install pytest -e .
          pytest tests/python -q

      - name: Install engine runtime (known-good ONNX set)
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # docs/ENGINE_RUNTIME_MATRIX.md: basic-pitch metadata
          # demands a nonexistent TensorFlow on Windows+3.12, so the
          # wheel goes in --no-deps and the ONNX dep set is explicit.
          pip download basic-pitch==0.4.0 --no-deps -d .work/bp_pkg
          pip install --no-deps .work/bp_pkg/basic_pitch-0.4.0-py2.py3-none-any.whl
          pip install onnxruntime librosa mir-eval "numpy<2" pretty-midi \
                      "resampy<0.4.3" scikit-learn scipy typing-extensions \
                      "setuptools<81" soundfile pyinstaller

      - name: Build frozen engine
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: python scripts/build_engine.py

      - name: Smoke-test frozen engine
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          # Handshake + one real offline Basic Pitch transcription —
          # a broken bundle fails here, not on a user's machine.
          python scripts/smoke_engine.py apps/desktop/src-tauri/resources/engine/hornscribe-engine.exe

      - name: Build NSIS installer (bundled engine)
        run: npm run tauri build -- --config src-tauri/tauri.bundled.json

      - name: Package portable zip
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # #244: the portable layout must ship the engine/ resource
          # dir next to the exe — engine.rs probes exe_dir/engine/.
          $exe = "src-tauri/target/release/hornscribe-desktop.exe"
          $engine = "src-tauri/resources/engine"
          $stage = "src-tauri/target/release/portable-stage"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $stage | Out-Null
          Copy-Item $exe $stage
          Copy-Item $engine "$stage/engine" -Recurse
          $zip = "src-tauri/target/release/HornScribe_${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}_x64-portable.zip"
          Compress-Archive -Path "$stage/*" -DestinationPath $zip -Force
          Get-Item $zip | Select-Object Name, Length

      - name: Verify artifacts contain the engine
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # The engine binary is ~130 MB — an installer or zip under
          # 50 MB cannot contain it (v0.1.0 shipped 4-5 MB assets).
          $installer = Get-Item src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/*-setup.exe
          $zip = Get-Item src-tauri/target/release/*-portable.zip
          if ($installer.Length -lt 50MB) { throw "installer too small to contain the engine: $($installer.Length)" }
          if ($zip.Length -lt 50MB) { throw "portable zip too small to contain the engine: $($zip.Length)" }
          Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
          $entries = [IO.Compression.ZipFile]::OpenRead($zip.FullName).Entries
          if (-not ($entries | Where-Object { $_.FullName -eq "engine/hornscribe-engine.exe" })) {
            throw "portable zip does not contain engine/hornscribe-engine.exe"
          }

      - name: Publish release assets
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          TAG="${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}"
          INSTALLER=$(ls src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/*-setup.exe)
          PORTABLE=$(ls src-tauri/target/release/*-portable.zip)
          if gh release view "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$TAG" "$INSTALLER" "$PORTABLE" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$TAG" "$INSTALLER" "$PORTABLE" \
              --title "HornScribe $TAG" \
              --notes-file ../../.github/RELEASE_NOTES.md \
              --prerelease
          fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Smoke-test a frozen HornScribe engine binary (#244).

Speaks the worker NDJSON protocol directly: handshake, then one real
offline transcription job over a generated sine-wave fixture.  The
release workflow runs this against hornscribe-engine.exe so a broken
bundle (missing ONNX model, missing librosa, protocol drift) fails CI
instead of shipping.

    python scripts/smoke_engine.py path/to/hornscribe-engine.exe

Exit 0 on success; prints the failing phase and exits 1 otherwise.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import queue
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import wave
from pathlib import Path

HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S = 120.0
JOB_TIMEOUT_S = 300.0


def _write_fixture(path: Path) -> None:
    """A440 sine with harmonics — enough pitched content for the
    backend to report notes."""
    sr = 22050
    frames = int(sr * 4.0)
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as fh:
        fh.setnchannels(1)
        fh.setsampwidth(2)
        fh.setframerate(sr)
        buf = bytearray()
        for i in range(frames):
            t = i / sr
            v = (
                0.6 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * 440.0 * t)
                + 0.2 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * 880.0 * t)
                + 0.1 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * 1320.0 * t)
            )
            buf += struct.pack("<h", int(v * 32000))
        fh.writeframes(bytes(buf))


def _request(proc: subprocess.Popen, method: str, payload: dict) -> None:
    line = json.dumps(
        {"v": 1, "kind": "request", "id": method, "method": method,
         "payload": payload},
    )
    assert proc.stdin is not None
    proc.stdin.write(line + "\n")
    proc.stdin.flush()


def _read_frame(proc: subprocess.Popen, timeout_s: float) -> dict:
    """Read one stdout frame with a deadline."""
    q: queue.Queue = queue.Queue()

    def pump() -> None:
        assert proc.stdout is not None
        line = proc.stdout.readline()
        q.put(line)

    threading.Thread(target=pump, daemon=True).start()
    try:
        line = q.get(timeout=timeout_s)
    except queue.Empty:
        raise TimeoutError(f"no frame within {timeout_s:.0f}s") from None
    if not line:
        raise RuntimeError("engine closed stdout")
    return json.loads(line)


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("usage: smoke_engine.py <path-to-hornscribe-engine>",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    engine = Path(sys.argv[1])
    if not engine.is_file():
        print(f"engine binary not found: {engine}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [str(engine)],
        stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=None,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
    )
    try:
        _request(proc, "engine.handshake", {"protocolVersion": 1})
        frame = _read_frame(proc, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S)
        if frame.get("error"):
            print(f"handshake error: {frame['error']}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        payload = frame.get("payload") or {}
        caps = payload.get("capabilities") or {}
        info = payload.get("engineInfo") or {}
        print(f"handshake ok: {info}")
        if not caps.get("basicPitchAvailable"):
            print("basic_pitch not importable inside the frozen engine",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            fixture = Path(td) / "fixture.wav"
            _write_fixture(fixture)
            _request(
                proc,
                "job.start",
                {
                    "jobKind": "transcription",
                    "params": {
                        "audioPath": str(fixture),
                        "tempoBpm": 120.0,
                        "meter": "4/4",
                        "texture": "mono",
                        "backend": "basicPitch",
                    },
                },
            )
            deadline = time.monotonic() + JOB_TIMEOUT_S
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                frame = _read_frame(
                    proc, max(1.0, deadline - time.monotonic())
                )
                if frame.get("kind") == "response":
                    if frame.get("error"):
                        print(f"job.start error: {frame['error']}",
                              file=sys.stderr)
                        return 1
                    continue
                evt = frame.get("payload") or {}
                phase = evt.get("phase")
                if phase in ("started", "progress"):
                    continue
                if phase == "completed":
                    result = evt.get("result") or {}
                    doc = result.get("scoreDocument") or {}
                    parts = (doc.get("content") or {}).get("parts")
                    notes = sum(
                        len(p.get("notes") or []) for p in (parts or [])
                    )
                    if not notes:
                        print("job completed with zero notes",
                              file=sys.stderr)
                        return 1
                    print(f"transcription ok: {notes} notes")
                    _request(proc, "engine.shutdown", {})
                    return 0
                print(f"job failed: {evt.get('error')}", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
            print("transcription job timed out", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
    finally:
        proc.kill()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
